reason: This passage (Exodus 14) depicts Yahweh actively protecting and saving the Hebrew people (Israelites). God instructs Moses to guide the people to safety, parts the Red Sea to enable their passage on dry ground with water walls protecting them on both sides, and delivers them from Egyptian pursuit by closing the waters on Pharaoh's army. Yahweh explicitly states He will be glorified through these acts of deliverance. The text shows Yahweh as protector and savior of Israel, demonstrating benevolence toward the Hebrew people, not antagonism. His antagonism is directed toward Egypt and Pharaoh, not toward Israel.
story: The Parting of the Red Sea
